title: Production attempt-log entries are stamped with at:"" — blank timestamps in the row log, result JSON, and warm-handoff email
evidence: sweep.gleam:164: `  Ok(run(db_conn, deps, "", sentry, default_batch_limit))`; sweep.gleam:171-173: "`now_iso` is an ISO-8601 timestamp string, or "" to let Postgres default to now() (production passes ""; tests pin the clock so cadence steps are deterministic)"; sweep.gleam:703-705: `fn outcome_entry(outcome: ChannelOutcome, at: String) -> json.Json {` / `  json.object([` / `    #("at", json.string(at)),`; messages.gleam:426: `  <> email_client.escape_html(entry.at)`
detail: The "" in bootstrap is meant for the due-SELECT clock, but the same now_iso is stamped as every attempt's `at`. Production thus stores blank timestamps for all T0/co-nudge/reminder entries; the warm-handoff email renders ": email, delivered" lines and result JSON attempts carry no times.
recommended_fix: Have main/bootstrap compute a real ISO-8601 timestamp (gleam_time) and pass it as now_iso — the SELECT accepts it and attempt entries get real `at` stamps; tests keep pinning their own.

title: Warm-handoff email renders a fabricated final attempt entry instead of the actual appended log (count + vocabulary mismatch)
evidence: sweep.gleam:527-536: `  let attempts =` / `    parse_attempts_entries(row.attempts)` / `    |> list.append([` / `      AttemptEntry(` / `        at: now_iso,` / `        channel: "email",` / `        outcome: "reminder_2",` / `        detail: "T+96h reminder",` / `      ),` / `    ])`; messages.gleam:65-69: `pub fn outcome_name(outcome: Outcome) -> String {` / `  case outcome {` / `    Delivered -> "delivered"` / `    Skipped -> "skipped"` / `    Failed -> "failed"`; messages.gleam:408: `      <> " times over the last 4 days. The attempt log:",`
detail: The advance already appended two real entries (email+sms, delivered/skipped/failed), but the render adds one hard-coded "email, reminder_2" line — an outcome outside the vocabulary. The email's count and log therefore do not match the row's log, contradicting §8.3's attempt-log render and the email's "the same log" copy.
recommended_fix: Build the render entries from the same `outcomes` list the advance appended (actual channel/outcome/detail), or re-read the row after the advance, instead of fabricating a mirror entry.

title: Warm-handoff notification can be permanently lost with no retry and no Sentry escalation
evidence: sweep.gleam:444-447: `    Ok(pog.Returned(_, [_])) -> {` / `      // Advance won — dispatch the warm handoff (exactly-once: only the` / `      // advance winner notifies). Best-effort: a dispatch failure is logged,` / `      // never fails the row (the reminder already sent).` / `      dispatch_warm_handoff(db, deps, now_iso, row, context)`; sweep.gleam:555-556: `      let _ =` / `        notification_dispatch.notify_reference_unreachable(`; notification_dispatch.gleam:658-663: `    Error(err) -> {` / `      wisp.log_warning(` / `        "Failed to create notification: " <> debug_query_error(err),` / `      )` / `      Error("Failed to create notification")` / `    }`
detail: The T+96 warm handoff is §8.3's only unreachable-path notification (T+144 is silent by design). A transient DB error at the in-app insert permanently drops it: the row is already at attempt_count=4, the Result is discarded, and dispatch() only log_warns — no Sentry, no retry. Siblings share the discard pattern, but there the state change itself is landlord-visible; here the notification IS the mechanism.
recommended_fix: Capture the notify_reference_unreachable Result: on Error, Sentry-capture + log it (mark_failed's pattern) so a dropped warm handoff escalates instead of vanishing into a warning line.
